  1. LLM inference services

LLM inference services

The llmInferenceServices list renders one LLMInferenceService per entry. Use it for generative models that need multi-node serving, disaggregated prefill and decode, LLM-aware routing, or request-driven autoscaling.

Unlike models, these entries do not use a ClusterServingRuntime. You define the container image and arguments directly.

Fields

Field Required Default Purpose
name Yes — Resource name
model Yes — Model block; model.uri is required
image No llmDefaults.image Container image for leader and worker
args No llmDefaults.args Container arguments
resources No llmDefaults.resources Requests and limits
replicas No llmDefaults.replicas Fixed replica count; ignored when scaling is set
parallelism No — Tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism
worker No — Presence enables multi-node serving
prefill No — Presence enables a separate prefill pool
router No llmDefaults.router Gateway, route, and scheduler configuration
scaling No — Autoscaling configuration; replaces replicas
baseRefs No — LLMInferenceServiceConfig references to compose
volumeMounts No llmDefaults.volumeMounts Mounts for the main container
labels No llmDefaults.labels Labels on the workload
annotations No llmDefaults.annotations Annotations on the workload
namespace No namespace Namespace override
injectHfToken No true Set false to skip HF_TOKEN injection

Pod fields

These render into the leader pod, and into the worker pod when worker is present. Each can also be set once in llmDefaults.

Group Fields
Scheduling nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity, topologySpreadConstraints, priorityClassName, schedulerName, nodeName
Identity serviceAccountName, automountServiceAccountToken, imagePullSecrets
Runtime runtimeClassName, securityContext, terminationGracePeriodSeconds, restartPolicy
Storage volumes, paired with volumeMounts on the container
Networking hostNetwork, hostIPC, shareProcessNamespace, dnsPolicy, dnsConfig, hostAliases
Init initContainers

A value set on an entry replaces the llmDefaults value rather than merging with it. Fields set in neither place are omitted so KServe applies its own default. false and 0 are honoured rather than treated as unset.

Minimal example 

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

This uses llmDefaults.image (vllm/vllm-openai:latest) and llmDefaults.args (--model /mnt/models).

The model block

model is passed through unchanged, so any field the CRD supports is available.

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
      name: llama-3.1-8b-instruct

model.name is the identifier clients send in the OpenAI-style model field. It defaults to the resource name.

Defaults 

llmDefaults:
  replicas: 1
  image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest
  args: [--model, /mnt/models]
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: "16"
      memory: 64Gi
  router:
    gateway: {}
    route: {}
    scheduler: {}

Pin the image in production. vllm/vllm-openai:latest changes without notice.

llmDefaults:
  image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0

The model is mounted at /mnt/models, so --model /mnt/models is correct for vLLM. Keep that argument when you override args.

Single-node GPU serving 

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --served-model-name
      - llama-3.1-8b
      - --max-model-len
      - "8192"
      - --dtype
      - bfloat16
    replicas: 2
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

Multi-node serving

Adding a worker key enables multi-node serving through LeaderWorkerSet. An empty map reuses the leader image, arguments, and resources.

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-70b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --tensor-parallel-size
      - "4"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "16"
        memory: 128Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "4"
    parallelism:
      tensor: 4
      data: 8
      dataLocal: 4
    worker: {}

data divided by dataLocal determines the node count. Above, 8 / 4 gives two nodes with four GPUs each.

Give workers a different shape when needed:

    worker:
      image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
      args:
        - --model
        - /mnt/models
        - --tensor-parallel-size
        - "4"
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "16"
          memory: 128Gi
          nvidia.com/gpu: "4"

Workers also accept the pod fields listed above, which is how you place leader and worker on different hardware:

    nodeSelector:
      accelerator: nvidia-h100
    worker:
      nodeSelector:
        accelerator: nvidia-a100
      priorityClassName: worker-priority

A worker field resolves in the order worker → entry → llmDefaults, so a worker that sets nothing inherits the leader’s placement.

worker: {} and omitting worker are different. An empty map still enables multi-node serving.

Multi-node serving requires the LeaderWorkerSet controller:

kubectl get crd leaderworkersets.leaderworkerset.x-k8s.io

Disaggregated prefill and decode

Separate the compute-bound prefill phase from the memory-bound decode phase. Adding a prefill key enables the pool, exactly like worker.

The simplest form reuses the workload’s image, arguments, resources, and placement:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b-disagg
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
    prefill: {}

Tune and place the prefill pool independently by setting fields inside prefill:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b-disagg
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --enforce-eager
    nodeSelector:
      accelerator: nvidia-a100
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
    prefill:
      replicas: 2
      args:
        - --model
        - /mnt/models
        - --enable-chunked-prefill
      nodeSelector:
        accelerator: nvidia-h100
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "16"
          memory: 64Gi
          nvidia.com/gpu: "2"

prefill accepts the same container keys as the workload (image, args, resources, volumeMounts, injectHfToken), the same pod fields, and its own replicas, parallelism, scaling, labels, and annotations. Anything unset falls back to the workload, then to llmDefaults.

HF_TOKEN is injected into the prefill containers on the same terms as the leader. Disable it for the prefill pool alone with prefill.injectHfToken: false.

Multi-node prefill

Adding prefill.worker spreads the prefill pool across nodes, mirroring the top-level worker:

    prefill:
      parallelism:
        tensor: 4
        data: 8
        dataLocal: 4
      worker: {}

Full control over the prefill container

Supplying containers under prefill.template replaces the generated container and is passed through verbatim, including any env you set:

    prefill:
      replicas: 2
      template:
        nodeSelector:
          accelerator: nvidia-h100
        containers:
          - name: main
            image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
            args: [--model, /mnt/models, --enable-chunked-prefill]
            env:
              - name: HF_TOKEN
                valueFrom:
                  secretKeyRef:
                    name: hf-secret
                    key: HF_TOKEN

The same escape hatch exists for the leader and worker through template.containers and worker.containers.

Routing

The default router requests a managed gateway, route, and scheduler:

llmDefaults:
  router:
    gateway: {}
    route: {}
    scheduler: {}

Attach to an existing gateway, or disable parts of the router:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    router:
      gateway:
        refs:
          - name: shared-gateway
            namespace: infrastructure
      route: {}
      scheduler: {}

See Networking and endpoints.

Autoscaling

Setting scaling removes the fixed replicas field from the rendered resource.

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    scaling:
      minReplicas: 1
      maxReplicas: 8

See Autoscaling.

Composing shared configuration

baseRefs references LLMInferenceServiceConfig objects, letting several workloads share a base definition.

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    baseRefs:
      - standard-gpu-profile

Enable the shipped configs when you use this pattern:

kserve-runtime-configs:
  kserve:
    llmisvcConfigs:
      enabled: true

Verifying 

kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models
kubectl describe llminferenceservice llama-8b -n models
kubectl get pods -n models -w
kubectl logs -n models -l app.kubernetes.io/name=llama-8b --tail=100

Calling the model 

kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-8b 8080:80

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-8b",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize Kubernetes in one sentence."}],
    "max_tokens": 128
  }'
